Initiated by the Research Data Alliance's I-ADOPT Working Group, the I-ADOPT Interoperability Framework is being further specified and implemented under the patronage of the GO FAIR Foundation, in collaboration with a broad community of international partners. Learn more on our [About](https://i-adopt.github.io/about.html) page.

## Understanding I-ADOPT
- Watch this video for a quick overview of the I-ADOPT framework.
{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8AB_OSA_CJk >}}

Applying the I-ADOPT Framework means:

1.  decompose the variable in atomic components
2.  assign a description role for each component
3.  annotate each component with concepts from terminologies

![](img/example.jpg)

This I-ADOPT decomposition and annotation exercise should result in a variable concept with its associated concepts in a SKOS vocabulary:

![](img/representation.jpg)

See [here](https://w3id.org/ozcar-theia/c_f120f651) the variable represented as SKOS concept from the [Theia/OZCAR Thesaurus](https://in-situ.theia-land.fr/skosmos/theia_ozcar_thesaurus/en/).

- Explore this [presentation](https://github.com/i-adopt/i-adopt.github.io/blob/main/material/EOV%20I-ADOPT.pdf) to understand how to decompose a variable. 


## Resources
* I-ADOPT Framework ontology <https://i-adopt.github.io/ontology/>
* [I-ADOPT Visualizer](https://sirkos.github.io/iadopt-vis/) enables to model and visualize variables according to the ontology
* I-ADOPT Corpus <https://i-adopt.github.io/Corpus/> contains 102 I-ADOPTed variables
* [I-ADOPT Variable Design Patterns](https://github.com/mabablue/I-ADOPT-patterns-playground) contains patterns for description components and decision trees to guide the modelling of I-ADOPT variables
* [I-ADOPT Roadmap](https://i-adopt.github.io/roadmap.html) gives an overview of achieved, ongoing and planned activities
* [I-ADOPT News](https://i-adopt.github.io/news.html): Subscribe for updates
